grain.note: The approved look (round 9). Levels are set per surface, then the whole is scaled by grain-overall, so buildings show 45% on screen. Each surface writes its level as it is drawn; the grain pass applies it once, fixed to the screen, faded by distance. Same in every district.

tokens.name: grain-overall
tokens.usage: Scales every level below.

tokens.name: grain-white
tokens.usage: Buildings, pavements, the bottom corners, outer lanes and the road beyond about 18 m (45% on screen).

tokens.name: grain-cab
tokens.usage: A broad soft oval of road round the taxi, fading out between about 13 and 18 m ahead (about 11% on screen).

tokens.name: grain-sky
tokens.usage: The sky (30% on screen).

tokens.name: grain-people
tokens.usage: The ghosted people on the pavements (45% on screen).

tokens.name: grain-taxi
tokens.usage: The player's taxi (about 11% on screen).

tokens.name: grain-vehicles
tokens.usage: Other traffic (about 11% on screen).

tokens.name: grain-signs
tokens.usage: Signs and lights: never grained.

picture.note: Fixed numbers of the street picture and its meter.

tokens.name: picture-height
tokens.usage: The street is drawn for a 540-line picture; its width follows the window (960 at 16:9, 1170 on a 2.17:1 phone), and the picture is scaled to fill.

tokens.name: meter-scale
tokens.usage: The meter is drawn at 82.5% of its round 9 size, shrunk towards its bottom-left corner (Barney, 28 October 2026).

tokens.name: meter-inset
tokens.usage: The meter's face sits 14 picture pixels from the left and bottom edges.

tokens.name: phone-label-min
tokens.usage: On phones the meter's row labels are drawn no smaller than 10 CSS px.

tokens.name: auto-smoothing-off
tokens.usage: Picture: Automatic turns edge smoothing off if frames come more than this far apart in the first seconds of play. A 60 Hz screen's frames are 16.7 ms apart, so 16 ms would trip on every device that keeps up (decided in the kit, phase 3).

tokens.name: auto-sharpness-down
tokens.usage: Picture: Automatic then draws at ordinary sharpness if frames still take longer than this.

tokens.name: pop-time
tokens.usage: The crash pop's whole life, from springing in to gone. A game's crash freeze can last longer: after the pop the frozen taxi and the vehicle it hit show for the rest of it (Barney, 29 October 2026).

tokens.name: pop-box
tokens.usage: The crash pop's box on a 720-line window, centred on the crash point and kept inside the picture. Scale it with the window's height.

tokens.name: bay-size
tokens.usage: The stop bay: 3 m across, 10 m along the kerbside lane, about twice the taxi's length. The stopping area.

tokens.name: lamp-time
tokens.usage: Roadworks lamps: each pair lit for half a second, then the other (once a second each, well under the flash limit).

tokens.name: wave-time
tokens.usage: A waiting passenger swaps between hailing and waving every 0.4 s until the taxi stops.

tokens.name: district-length
tokens.usage: Each of the four districts, so the whole street is about 15 km: long enough for a zone of five fares (about 190 s of clock at 70 km/h).

tokens.name: pin-size
tokens.usage: The pin over where the taxi is heading, on a 720-line window; on phones never smaller than 0.6 of that in CSS pixels (24 by 35).

tokens.name: badge-size
tokens.usage: A power-up badge under the taxi on a 720-line window (39px with 快's ring); on phones never smaller than 19 CSS pixels.

tokens.name: ring-fade
tokens.usage: The bay's ring fades in once three-quarters of the taxi is inside the bay, and out once the stop has counted.

tokens.name: receipt-time
tokens.usage: The receipt slip: prints up out of the meter in 0.25 s, holds 2 s, goes back in 0.25 s. The caption steps aside meanwhile.

tokens.name: shield-box
tokens.usage: The SAFE! sign (the shielded hit) on a 720-line window, centred over the point of contact; it lives for pop-time.

tokens.name: zone-time
tokens.usage: The zone change: 0.4 s in, 1 s on the district just finished, 0.6 s across to the next, 1 s on it, 0.4 s back to play.
